subject: Questionnaire routing and evidence scan for HelixHealth Labs
messages:
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questionnaire routing and evidence scan for HelixHealth Labs

Hi Alex / Maya,

Thanks again for your time on the demo this morning — appreciate the straight questions. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can kick off the security intake: 

- Scope I heard: SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA/PHI in-scope, US data residency, and Helix’s vendor questionnaire (attached).
- Options for us to provide answers: we can (A) complete a CAIQ/SIG prefills and map those answers back to your sheet, or (B) return your custom questionnaire with evidence links and short narrative answers. Either works — pick whichever your team prefers.

Action items / asks for you:
1) Please confirm whether you want option A (CAIQ mapping) or B (direct custom file completion).
2) Confirm the list of evidence you require (typical asks below).
3) If PHI is in-scope confirm procurement contact for a BAA — we can circulate a DocuSign BAA once timelines are agreed.

Typical evidence we attach: SOC2 Type II report, architecture/dataflow diagram, encryption/KMS details, control owner contacts, data retention policy. I attached our SOC2 summary and a dataflow PNG for your review.

Proposed timeline: kickoff call (30 min) next week, then 5-10 business days to return a fully mapped questionnaire and evidence bundle depending on number of controls in scope.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf (redacted), redwood_architecture_dataflow.png

If you confirm option and PHI scope I’ll get Jordan to schedule a kickoff and route the BAA.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@helixhealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <m.singh@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questionnaire routing and evidence scan for HelixHealth Labs

Thanks Karthik — good recap. A few clarifying questions from our security and procurement teams after the demo:

- Helix prefers to start with our custom questionnaire (attached: Helix_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx) because it maps directly into our intake tracker. That said, we’re open to you providing a CAIQ mapping if that is faster for you and you can indicate where each CAIQ answer maps into our sheet.

- Required controls we need explicit evidence for: encryption at rest (KMS / key rotation policy), encryption in transit (TLS versions), RBAC and admin separation, logging/retention (SIEM evidence), vulnerability management (scan cadence), incident response runbook, and a current SOC2 Type II report.

- PHI: yes, PHI will be in scope for the POC. Procurement will require a signed BAA before we share any production data. Contact for procurement is Maya Singh (cc).

- Data residency: we need confirmation that data for our POC can be restricted to US-only regions (us-east-us-west preference). If that requires Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment, please highlight the difference in cost and lead time.

Can you confirm those points and let us know whether option A or B is preferable from your side? We attached our questionnaire for your intake team to review.

Regards,
Alex Turner
Head of Security Operations | HelixHealth Labs
alex.turner@helixhealth.com
Attachment: Helix_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@helixhealth.com>
Cc: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Maya Singh <m.singh@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questionnaire routing and evidence scan for HelixHealth Labs

Alex — thanks, clear notes. Short answers and proposed path: 

1) Questionnaire approach: we can do both, but recommend option A (CAIQ/SIG prefills + mapping) for speed. We’ll fill the CAIQ where applicable and provide a crosswalk showing which CAIQ question maps to each line in your sheet. If you prefer the completed custom spreadsheet, we can return that instead — we’ll just need a little extra time to attach inline evidence.

2) Evidence: we will provide the SOC2 Type II report (redacted), an architecture/dataflow diagram, KMS details (provider, rotation cadence), TLS configs, a summary of RBAC/SCIM integrations, and contact info for control owners. If you need raw logs or SIEM exports we’ll discuss export method and retention.

3) PHI and residency: PHI is supported. For a standard hosted account we can route PII/PHI to a US-only region (us-east-1) but for strict residency or dedicated hardware we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private — I put estimated lead times below:
   - Hosted (region-restricted): typically immediate at provisioning, no infra change.
   - Dedicated: 2-4 weeks provisioning plus contract lead time.
   - Private/on-prem: variable (multi-week), requires Ops coordination.

4) Timeline: if you choose option A we can return a CAIQ-prefill + crosswalk in ~5 business days. For option B (direct custom completion with embedded evidence) plan ~8-12 business days.

Next step: Jordan will propose a 30-min intake call to confirm control owners and evidence locations. Please confirm preferred option (A or B) and available times for a kick-off next week.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf (redacted), redwood_architecture_dataflow.png

Thanks,
Karthik

Quick logistics note — happy to own scheduling and the evidence bundle once we agree the approach. Typical playbook: 

- Owner assignment and evidence list (Day 0) — Helix confirms required evidence set and control owners.
- Redwood performs CAIQ prefills and maps answers (5 business days target) or completes custom sheet with evidence links (8-12 business days).
- We’ll deliver a single evidence bundle (Drive folder) with named artifacts and short README.

If PHI is in scope we’ll circulate a DocuSign BAA to your procurement team (Maya) so we can enable the POC environment. Can you confirm an internal procurement contact for the BAA signature?

I’ll put some time options for the intake call into your calendars once you confirm pref.

—Jordan Blake
